short: Income and expenses over a period, ending in profit or loss.
seoTitle: What Is Profit and Loss Statement? Meaning and Example
metaDescription: A profit and loss statement summarises income and expenses over a period and arrives at profit or loss. The P&L is the fastest read on whether trading works.
definition: A profit and loss statement summarises income and expenses over a period and arrives at profit or loss. It runs from revenue through cost of goods sold to gross profit, then through operating expenses to net profit.
bodyHtml:
Why Profit and Loss Statement matters

The P&L is the fastest read on whether trading works. Compared month against month, it also shows which specific cost has drifted, rather than just that money is tight.

How Profit and Loss Statement works in practice

Compare each line as a percentage of sales, not only in rupees, so growth-driven increases are distinguishable from real cost creep. Read it beside the cash flow statement, since profit and cash rarely move together.

faq.question: Is the P&L the same as cash flow?
faq.answer: No. It records income when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of when money moves.

faq.question: What period should a P&L cover?
faq.answer: Monthly for management, quarterly for trends, annually for statutory reporting.
